memory_candidates.content: To demonstrate a regression fixture 'fails first' against a pre-fix version of a script without ever hand-editing the real source-store file in place, build a standalone scratch probe: copy the entire scripts directory to a scratch path, overwrite just the one target script with a surgically-reverted copy (python3 string-slice removal of the exact landed block, verified by bash -n for syntax), and write a small driver script that reuses the real suite's helper functions (build_repo, write_progress, run_phase_commit) but points SRC_SCRIPTS_DIR at the scratch copy. Run the new assertions against both the scratch copy (expect fail) and the real script (expect pass), then discard the scratch probe entirely. This keeps the demonstration and the deliverable fully separated, with git diff on the real file staying empty throughout.

When a phase edit to a context/standards doc changes its line count, a repo that maintains a regenerated context index (index-entries.json) with cached line_count fields will show that index file as dirty after the next deploy-headless.sh run, even though it was never named in the phase's own file_scope. Since it is a derived artifact outside any one task's declared territory, git-commit-scoped.sh's V10 containment refuses it under --task attribution (rc=2, zero positive pathspecs remain). The sanctioned landing path is to omit --task entirely on that one commit -- V10 (and V5) are --task opt-in only, so omitting it reproduces the same no-task-context commit path already used for repo-wide maintenance commits (e.g. roadmap regeneration), skipping containment and contention checks by design rather than by workaround.

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check
sapience_notes.value: The own-task-directory and engine-written-state carve-outs work by ADMITTING the task directory, specs/TODO.md, and specs/state.json as explicit members of the file_scope_arr array is_contained() iterates -- they pass containment because they are tested and matched, not because the predicate skips them. Only the --plan-path entry is genuinely untested, via a separate stage_paths append.

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-phase.sh completeness-check disarmament
sapience_notes.value: When a phase's sole self-reported files_touched entry is dropped by the Containment Self-Check, files_touched empties to zero entries and run_completeness_check flips to false -- the post-commit exit-6 completeness gate is silently skipped for that commit, not merely noisy. This is the real cost of a false-positive containment drop: a disabled safety gate, not data loss (the unconditional task_dir/ stage_paths seed still lands the file).

sapience_notes.subject: positive-observable technique for a silent post-action gate
sapience_notes.value: To prove a post-commit completeness check RAN (rather than being silently skipped by an upstream filter that emptied its input), plant a .git/hooks/pre-commit that reverts one target path inside the temporary partial index via git update-index --cacheinfo <pre-commit-blob-sha> <path>. The check then exits non-zero naming that path if and only if it ran -- strictly stronger than asserting the absence of skip-family warning strings (via-negativa).

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-scoped.sh's V5/V10 opt-in gating
sapience_notes.value: Both the V5 contended-path refusal and the V10 file_scope-containment guard inside git-commit-scoped.sh are strictly --task opt-in: omitting --task entirely skips both checks, which is the sanctioned (not a workaround) commit path for a repo-wide derived/maintenance artifact that falls outside any single task's declared file_scope, such as a regenerated context-index entry.

sapience_notes.subject: test-git-commit-phase.sh fixture family for own-task-directory paths
sapience_notes.value: Case 40's dotfile-at-task-directory-root fixtures (.return-meta.json, .orchestrator-handoff.json) needed no code change to pass, because is_contained()'s containment test is plain bash case-pattern matching ("$entry"/* against the admitted task_dir/ entry) rather than filesystem glob expansion -- a leading dot in a basename is not a separate code path for that predicate.

sapience_notes.subject: task 535's originating defect
sapience_notes.value: The dispatch's own code-level diagnosis (an is_contained() carve-out gap dropping a task's own plan artifact) had already been fixed in the source store before this dispatch began; the remaining, genuine defect was purely documentary -- a standards sentence claiming the carve-out paths were 'never tested... structurally outside its reach' when in fact three of the four are tested and admitted, only the --plan-path entry being genuinely untested.
